threepl.netlist

Class GenFunctions

  • java.lang.Object
    • threepl.netlist.TDECode
      • threepl.netlist.GenFunctions
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    TDEConstants, NetConstants, Constant
    Direct Known Subclasses:
    XElements

    public abstract class GenFunctions
extends TDECode
implements Constant, TDEConstants

    This class contains general methods for handling nets, net and signal variable arguments and lists, net interconnection and some string formatting methods. The 'args' methods convert single Net arguments or an array of Net into an ArrayList so that these functions can be called with these argument types without having 3 different calling signatures for each function.

    This method is also the super class for EDIF code generation.

    The arguments and return values are not a consistent scheme through all elements.

     The class structure is -

        TDECode           implementation of TDE modules - vendor independent
           |
      GenFunctions        general support methods - vendor independent
           |
       XElements          Xilinx general unified elements
           |
       XFunctions         Xilinx higher level functions
           |
       XTDECode           Xilinx implementation of TDE modules
           |
     ----------------------------
    /   /  |   \   \      \
 XC2S XCV XC3S XC2V XC2VP XC4V ......     Xilinx elements specific to FPGA families
    All classes above starting with "X" are in subdirectory "xilinx".

    All methods in the lowest subclasses override corresponding methods in class XElements which throw exceptions to pick up the use of special elements in FPGA families which do not have them.

    TDE code generation methods are invoked using the FPGA family as the object instance.

      • sig_expand

        public static Net[] sig_expand(Net[] s,
                               int n,
                               boolean signed)
        Pad a net array at the MS end, if required, to expand it to the specified size. If the input net array is already the specified size it is simply returned. If padding is required it will be zeros for unsigned or the sign bit of the input if signed.
        Parameters:
        s - is the input net array
        n - is the required size
        signed - is true if the array is signed
        Returns:
        the expanded net array

      • sig_expand

        public static Net[] sig_expand(Net s,
                               int n,
                               boolean dupl)
        Expand a single net to a net array. If the last argument is true the net is duplicated into an array of the specified size. If the last argument is false the array is padded with Net.LO.
        Parameters:
        s - is the input net
        n - is the required size
        dupl - is true the net is duplicated
        Returns:
        the expanded net array

      • connect

        public static void connect(Net[] dest,
                           Net[] src,
                           boolean signextend)
        Connect two Net arrays with truncation or padding. If the destination Net array is smaller than the source Net array the most significant source Nets are ignored (truncation). If the destination Net array is larger than the source Net array the extra destination bits are connected to GND if there is no sign extension, or to the most significant source Net array bit if sign extension is required (padding).
        Parameters:
        dest - is the destination Net array
        src - is the source Net array
        signextend - is true if sign extension is required
